findings.claim: The two append arms are whole-file replacements carrying 'the user's bytes plus ours'.
findings.counterexample: existing comes from fs.readFileSync(hookPath,'utf-8') at :1525, so writeFileAtomicSync(hookPath, existing + separator + appendBlock) re-encodes every invalid byte as U+FFFD; executed through the built installGitHook, a user pre-commit containing 0xE9 comes back as EF BF BD (action 'appended') where the pre-fold fs.appendFileSync preserved it - the exact silent-corruption class eject.ts:253-259 was ruled to skip-with-reason on .git/hooks/* in the mmnto-ai/totem#2620 falsification round.

findings.claim: The attested extension is carried through byte-for-byte (changeset :9, docs/wiki/hook-integration.md:31).
findings.counterexample: rewritten = hookContent + trailerTailAfterEndMarker(existing, trailerStart) is built from the same utf-8 decode at :1525, so a trailer containing any non-UTF-8 byte is rewritten as U+FFFD rather than byte-for-byte; upgradePrePushHookIfNeeded has the identical exposure with user lines on both sides (:2434 read, :2500 write).

findings.claim: Hook writes carry the atomic helper's declared boundaries, all of them now named.
findings.counterexample: packages/core/src/fs-atomic.ts declares five, and the omitted one is the only silent failure - hard-link identity is not preserved: rename-over replaces the directory entry, so a target with nlink > 1 silently decouples from its other names - newly reachable because this fold converts the two append arms, the post-merge create and the four .sh helpers from in-place writes (which updated every hard-link name) to rename-over.

findings.claim: The helper's declared boundaries are 'none of which occur in a repo the user owns and works in'.
findings.counterexample: The same sentence then lists 'after a hard kill mid-write a <hook>.<pid>-<uuid8>.tmp can remain beside the hook', which does occur in a repo the user owns and works in; the defensible claim is that none of them loses a byte, not that none of them occurs.

findings.claim: fs.statSync(hookPath).ino is a sound identity for the rename control on every platform CI runs.
findings.counterexample: Measured on win32 over 400 write/atomic-rewrite pairs, 400/400 of the returned ino values exceed 2^53 and 400/400 differ from the bigint value (double spacing 16-32 at those magnitudes), so two file IDs within ~8-16 would compare equal; 0/400 actually collided, and { bigint: true } retires the class for one word.

verdict: 1 BLOCKING, 2 MATERIAL, 2 MINOR over d2b11792 (the fold that made every git-hook write atomic); all five folded in 8a35423a. f8 was a regression the previous fold introduced: building the whole-file replacement from the UTF-8 decode re-encoded a user's non-round-tripping bytes as U+FFFD, executed through the built dist. Cure: the hook is read raw once, the decoded text serves the probes only, the append arms concatenate bytes, the block rewrite slices the trailer from the raw file after proving the managed region round-trips, the legacy pre-push upgrader declines a non-round-tripping hook (its ruled silent false), both inode reads are bigint, and the changeset names the hard-link boundary. Byte-level tests pin the append and the rewrite. The fold rewires the write path again, so the leg was re-armed on 8a35423a (its own deposit).
